Developers urged to create more family-friendly spaces, malls and homes; AC framework updated
article:
Real estate developers and mall owners in Singapore are being called on to provide more family-friendly spaces and amenities in their projects.

Support for marriage and parenthood in Singapore requires a whole-of-society approach, said Indranee Rajah, Second Minister for Finance and National Development, and Minister in the Prime Minister's Office.

Speaking at the Real Estate Developers’ Association of Singapore (Redas) Mid-Autumn Lunch on Sept 23, she noted that the real estate sector — as developers, property owners and landlords, as well as employers — has a meaningful role to play in helping to reverse the downward trend for marriage and parenthood.

Developers have a significant say in how buildings are designed and what features and amenities are provided.

They could thus include intentional and inclusive spaces for families in their projects — whether it be more family-friendly common spaces, lactation rooms or facilities in commercial buildings, and spaces that cater to young children and elderly grandparents alike.

When it comes to malls, Indranee cited feedback from families seeking more common areas where parents can wait for children or seniors, as well as more family-friendly activities.

She urged mall owners to consider their properties as potential community hubs, with activities for singles and families, while encouraging their F&B tenants to adopt more family-friendly features and practices.

At the event, Redas president Tan Swee Yiow similarly highlighted the role developers can play.

Many of the association’s members build the homes that young families move into and the spaces around them, including playgrounds, gardens, communal decks and flexible multigenerational layouts.

"When we get these spaces right, we help families meet their aspirations, whatever shape that family takes," Tan said.

He also floated several ideas for consideration, while clarifying that they are not formal Redas positions.

"For larger developments, perhaps we could allocate a small percentage of units as larger, family-sized homes."

He also suggested exempting gross floor area (GFA) for household shelters so the space could be used to reintroduce helper’s rooms into floor plans, as well as providing more childcare facilities near homes and offices with similar GFA exemptions.

"It takes a village to raise a child. Government, employers, developers and society all have a part to play," Tan said. "We can help more Singaporeans start and grow the families they hope for."

Accredited Checker framework enhanced

Separately, Indranee announced at the event that the government will enhance the Accredited Checker (AC) framework to better support structural design checks.

This is especially for larger, more complex or higher-risk projects.

ACs and ACOs provide independent reviews of structural designs, to ensure the structural integrity of a building and the safety of designs early in the planning stage.

From September 2028, ACs and Accredited Checker Organisations (ACOs) who undertake larger and more complex projects will be required to demonstrate relevant recent checking and design experience, as well as a good track record.

Requirements for smaller and lower-risk projects will be calibrated according to the risks involved, so that individual ACs can continue to take on such projects.

These changes are intended to give developers greater confidence that complex projects are being checked by professionals and organisations with the expertise, personnel and resources required.

Besides, stronger checks upstream will help reduce downstream design issues and rectification costs, Indranee noted.

A two-year transition period will be provided before full implementation in September 2028, and contracts awarded before then will not be affected.

In addition, from 2028 onwards, the Building and Construction Authority will extend the registration and renewal validity for ACs, ACOs and Specialist ACs from 12 months to 36 months to reduce administrative burden.

The Association of Consulting Engineers Singapore has also developed a Value Articulation Framework for AC checking services.

This is meant to give developers and ACs or ACOs a common and transparent basis to discuss the checking approach and resources required for each project. It will help developers assess AC proposals more holistically, based on factors beyond fees alone.

As building works become more complex, it is essential for ACs and ACOs to be equipped with the technical capability, organisational resources and relevant experience to carry out robust and effective checks, Indranee said.

title: $38 mil price tag on Mohamed Sultan Rd commercial, serviced apartment buildings
article:
A freehold mixed-use development with approval for Serviced Apartment (SA1) use has been put on the market with a guide price of about $38 million, or around $2,621 psf on the existing floor area of 14,497 sq ft.

Located at 22 and 23 Mohamed Sultan Road, the assets comprise a serviced apartment block and a commercial building, sitting on separate land parcels with a combined land area of about 4,221 sq ft.

Both are fully tenanted and able to provide stable and immediate rental income to incoming investors, according to exclusive marketing agent CBRE in a Sept 23 media release.

“The assets are well-maintained and in excellent condition, offering a turnkey investment with minimal near-term capital expenditure required,” said Clemence Lee, CBRE executive director of capital markets, Singapore.

Co-living operator Cove is currently managing apartments, lofts and rooms with shared amenities at both properties.

The rear block, at 22 Mohamed Sultan Road, is an eight-storey development approved for SA1 use, housing serviced apartment units on levels two to eight.

It occupies a 3,075 sq ft site zoned for residential use with a gross plot ratio of 3.8 based on the URA Master Plan 2025.

The front block, at 23 Mohamed Sultan Road, is a four-storey building with a basement. It has a shop in the basement, restaurant on the ground floor, and serviced apartments from levels two to four.

That block sits on a land plot spanning 1,146 sq ft, zoned for commercial use.

Online checks show that Bad Habits, which serves New York-style pizzas by the slice, occupies the ground floor of the front block.

Lee noted that such freehold, income-producing mixed-use assets in River Valley are tightly held, while the Singapore River-Robertson Quay district is also undergoing renewal.

The properties are a seven-minute walk to Fort Canning MRT Station and an eight-minute drive to Raffles Place in the CBD and the Orchard Road shopping district.

The sale will be conducted via an expression of interest exercise, which closes at 3pm on Oct 28.

title: 3 Singapore Stocks That Could Lead the Next Market Rally
article:
The
Straits Times Index
(SGX: ^STI)’s strong year-to-date (YTD) rally of more than 20% has rewarded investors who stayed invested.
After this first wave of gains, investors tend to start hunting for whatever may lead the next leg – and that’s rarely the stocks that have already run the hardest.
The better candidates are businesses whose earnings could accelerate, valuations still leave room to re-rate, or have catalysts that could shift how the market sees them.
Here are three.
What Could Drive the Next Singapore Market Rally?
Lower interest rates could cut financing costs and support valuations for income-generating assets.
Stronger corporate earnings give any rally a more durable foundation than sentiment alone.
Improving investor sentiment could pull more capital into Singapore equities generally.
And, finally, sector rotation, where money is shifted into laggards with better forward prospects, could also fund the next leg up for the market.
That said, momentum alone won’t be enough; the next leaders need real catalysts behind them.
Seatrium Limited (SGX: 5E2) – The Earnings Growth Leader
Seatrium’s latest numbers for the first half of 2026 (1H2026) show genuine business inflection.
Revenue grew a modest 5% year on year (YoY) to S$5.6 billion, but that’s only part of the story: gross profit rose 22% to S$482 million, and gross margin ticked up to 8.6% from 7.4% a year ago.
The strong follow-through to earnings is best seen in Seatrium’s EBITDA surging 60% to S$651 million and net profit (excluding divestment) jumping 54% to S$212 million.
Seatrium’s return on equity (ROE) was also decent at 7.8%.
The company’s future growth looks bright, with a net order book of S$13.3 billion as of 30 June 2026.
Adding new contracts to this order backlog and continuing the decent showing of expanding profit margins could lead to further earnings growth and a higher share price correspondingly.
To cap things off,
Seatrium
trades at a reasonable forward price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of 15x, against a historical three-year average of 32x.
UOB Group Holdings (SGX: U11) – The Undervalued Blue Chip
Compared to its local bank peers,
DBS
(SGX: D05) and
OCBC
(SGX: O39), UOB’s share price return has trailed.
But UOB currently has a decent valuation with a price-to-book (P/B) ratio of 1.3x, which is the same as the three-year historical average.
Moreover, UOB’s P/B ratio is significantly lower than DBS’ 3.1x and OCBC’s 2.2x.
Despite the valuation discount, UOB has continued to deliver in both earnings and balance sheet strength.
Net profit after tax rose 10% YoY to S$1.5 billion in 1H2026, even though the net interest margin (NIM) declined by 0.17 percentage points to 1.74%.
UOB’s non-performing loans (NPL) ratio is healthy at 1.6%, while it sports a fully phased-in common equity tier 1 (CET1) ratio of 15%.
This affords UOB plenty of room to grow its recent dividend of S$0.88 per share for 1H2026.
Keppel DC REIT (SGX: AJBU) – The Structural Growth Play
Data centre demand tied to AI and cloud computing is about as clean a structural growth trend as exists on the
Singapore Exchange
(SGX: S68).
Keppel DC REIT, or KDC REIT, is Singapore’s largest pure-play vehicle for it, with 25 data centres across 10 countries.
For 1H2026, KDC REIT’s distributable income grew 18.5% YoY to S$150.7 million, and distribution per unit (DPU) rose 11.3% to S$0.05714.
The portfolio’s rental reversion came in around 10%, through renewals in Singapore and Australia, with the weighted average lease to expiry (WALE) extended to 6.7 years from 6.5 years a quarter ago.
Meanwhile, gearing is low at 34%, which gives real financial flexibility to the REIT to acquire more data centres and strengthen its earnings profile.
What Could Stop the Rally?
A global economic slowdown would hit all three, though unevenly.
Higher-for-longer interest rates
would particularly pressure KDC REIT’s valuation and UOB’s re-rating case.
Weakening corporate earnings would undercut Seatrium’s margin story specifically.
Geopolitical uncertainty (already visible in Seatrium’s Middle East-related disruption) is a live risk.
And after a strong run, profit-taking or valuations simply running ahead of fundamentals could stall any of the three regardless of how good the underlying business is.
Should You Buy Before the Next Rally?
Don’t chase what’s already rallied hardest – by definition, less upside remains once expectations are elevated.
Look for earnings before momentum: strong fundamentals are a better foundation than recent price action alone.
Consider staggering purchases rather than deploying all capital at once, since timing any rally precisely is close to impossible.
And keep
valuation
in perspective – even an excellent business can produce poor returns if bought at too high a price.
What Should Investors Monitor From Here?
For all three: quarterly earnings, management guidance, analyst revisions, and valuation changes relative to history.
For Seatrium specifically: new contract wins against that S$32 billion pipeline, and whether margin gains hold once one-off items roll off.
For UOB: The dividend growth, any signs of re-rating in the P/B multiple, and Greater China credit trends.
For KDC REIT: occupancy (watch the Cardiff vacancy that dented 1H2026’s headline number), further acquisitions, and DPU growth sustaining above its historical mid-single-digit pace.
Get Smart: The Next Winners May Already Be on Your Watchlist
Market rallies
create new winners as capital rotates between sectors.
Seatrium, UOB and Keppel DC REIT shouldn’t be judged on how far they’ve already run, but on whether their earnings, cash flows and structural positioning can support another leg higher – and on the evidence so far, all three have a genuine, if different, case.
The next market leader may not be the stock making the most noise today.
It could be the one whose fundamentals are just beginning to catch up with its potential.

title: Incredible Holdings seeks to be placed under judicial management
article:
Incredible Holdings has filed an application in the High Court to be placed under judicial management on Sept 21. The company has also asked for judicial managers, Ellyn Tan Huixian and Terrence Chin Khee Loon of Forvis Mazars Consulting Pte. Ltd., to be appointed to manage its affairs, business and property.

Under section 95 of the Insolvency, Restructuring and Dissolution Act 2018, an automatic moratorium will take place from the filing of the application up to the date which the application is decided by the court.

During this period, no order may be made for the winding up of the company. No one is also allowed to enforce any security over the company’s property or repossess any goods under any hire-purchase agreement, chattels leasing agreement, or retention of title agreement, unless the court allows it.

No other proceedings may be commenced or continued except with the permission of the court and no enforcement order or other legal process may be issued, continued or executed. No distress may be levied against the company or its property as well, except with the court’s permission.

The news comes days after the company announced that its independent director was interviewed by the Commercial Affairs Department (CAD) and the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) in relation to the company’s affairs.

As at 2.13pm, shares in Incredible Holdings are trading flat at 0.2 cents.

title: Singapore inflation up for third month to highest since 2024
article:
(Sept 23): Singapore inflation accelerated for a third month in a row to the highest in almost two years, pushing prices closer to the upper end of the central bank’s forecast range.

Core inflation, which excludes housing and private transportation costs, accelerated in August to 2.2% from a year earlier, the Singapore Department of Statistics said Wednesday. That’s the highest since September 2024 and matches the median estimate in a Bloomberg survey.

Food, retail and services saw faster inflation, according to a joint release by the Monetary Authority of Singapore and the Ministry of Trade and Industry, as elevated global oil prices and other external cost pressures continued to filter through to the economy.

“Global oil prices remain high and volatile while adverse weather conditions are expected to lower agricultural yields,” MAS and MTI said. As higher input costs pass through global supply chains, the prices of Singapore’s imported goods and services are expected to pick up in the quarters ahead, they said.

Against that backdrop, the authorities said “the risks to the inflation outlook remain tilted to the upside”.

See also: Higher costs of capital due to AI and fiscal risks could test financial system: MAS

The MAS forecasts core inflation at 1.5%-2.5% this year, seeing price pressures likely to moderate discernibly from around mid-2027.

The MAS, which tightened policy at its past two meetings this year, will announce its next decision mid-October. Several major central banks, including the Federal Reserve, Bank of Japan and European Central Bank, have raised rates recently to contain resurgent inflation.

“Singapore’s monetary policy appears to be in a good place,” said DBS Group Holdings Ltd economist Chua Han Teng. “We see its policy framework providing flexibility to lean against higher imported costs through calibrated adjustments if necessary amid an uncertain landscape of upside inflation risks.”

See also: Global reserves shift from dollar overstated, NY Fed study says

The all-items inflation rate came in at 2.3%, also meeting the median survey estimate. Utilities and other fuels rose 6.1%, the department’s data showed.

The government has sought to cushion the city-state from external shocks, rolling out nearly S$2 billion of support since the outbreak of the US-Iran war earlier this year.

title: Modi plans Canada trip for trade deal, speeds up Mexico talks
article:
(Sept 23): India is accelerating trade talks with Canada and Mexico as the three economies seek new markets and partners in response to the disruption unleashed by US President Donald Trump’s tariff policies.

Negotiators from India and Canada plan to hold a fifth round of talks from Oct 5, building on discussions that concluded last week, according to people familiar with the matter. A deal is likely to be inked in December when Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi is expected to visit Canada, the Globe and Mail reported, citing New Delhi’s envoy Dinesh Patnaik.

Separately, New Delhi is finalising a framework with Mexico to begin formal trade negotiations, the people said, asking not to be identified as the discussions are private. Officials are seeking to make faster progress in the trade talks as all three countries look to diversify their commercial ties, they said.

India’s Ministry of Commerce and Industry didn’t respond to a request for comment. Mexico’s Economy Ministry, which oversees the country’s trade negotiations, said there’s ongoing analysis for a potential deal although there is no concrete or final proposal yet.

The three economies, with combined economic output of more than US$8 trillion, are grappling with disruption from Trump’s trade policies. Mexico is scrambling to reach an agreement with the US as the two sides negotiate changes to their existing pact while Canada-US talks collapsed last month. The US is by far the biggest export market for both Canada and Mexico.

See also: Traders eye Xi-Trump meet for clues on AI rivalry, yuan outlook

India, meanwhile, is contending with fresh tariff threats from a new law that gives Trump the power to impose levies of as much as 100% on countries that purchase Russian oil and gas. New Delhi reached an interim trade deal with the US earlier this year and has been locked in negotiations over the tariff rate.

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney on Tuesday confirmed Modi’s visit to the country in December, around the time the Indian leader is expected to head to the Group of 20 meeting in Miami. Carney described Canada’s relationship with India as “exceptionally important” and that trade talks have proceeded well — echoing comments from his trade minister, Maninder Sidhu, in an interview on Bloomberg TV this week.

India’s push into Canada and Mexico builds on a burst of trade diplomacy that officials have touted as giving the country greater access to overseas markets. New Delhi has struck agreements with the UK, Oman and New Zealand over the past year and concluded long-running negotiations with the European Union while pursuing talks with a growing list of other economies.

See also: India warns US oil sanctions bill could hurt bilateral ties

India’s two-way trade with Canada and Mexico stood at nearly US$8 billion each in 2025-26.

Mexico is seeking greater access to India’s market for its alcoholic beverage tequila, fruit and auto components, people familiar with the matter said. New Delhi, meanwhile, wants Mexico to lower barriers on goods like automobiles, auto parts and steel, they said. Last year, Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum’s administration imposed tariffs of between 5% and 50% on steel and other products from Asian nations that don’t have a trade deal with Mexico.

India is looking to conclude a limited preferential trade agreement comprising only a small number of goods, the people said. The terms of negotiations are likely to be signed soon and the two sides expect talks to conclude by December, they said.

title: Chinese car brands hit record European share on hybrid demand
article:
(Sept 23): Chinese automakers grabbed another record share of Europe’s car market last month, luring buyers still wary about going fully electric with more affordable hybrid vehicles.

Brands including BYD Co made up nearly 12% of total new-car sales in the region in August, according to Dataforce. They accounted for one in four sales of all hybrids — or one in three for hybrids with a plug — as they cash in on models that are not subject to steep European Union tariffs.

The data show how China’s carmakers are capitalising on lingering consumer concern around charging networks and driving range, with hybrids acting as a stepping-stone to going fully electric. Still, surging fuel prices are piling pressure on the finances of combustion-engine car owners.

Demand for battery and hybrid cars jumped 27% in August, according to Dataforce, to offset declines for vehicles that only run on fuel. Thanks to EV gains, the overall market rose 4.6%.

Chinese hybrid vehicles do not currently face the same steep European Union tariffs as electric-vehicle imports from the country, though they may soon be hit with similar duties, Handelsblatt has reported. Germany is preparing a package of economic security measures that may include new tariffs on hybrids which it plans to present to the EU, Bloomberg reported this month.

See also: US investments in Spain surge 84% despite political tensions

In the UK, Chinese carmakers do not face the additional tariffs on EVs currently in place in the EU. There, more than one in five new cars is Chinese, with brands like Chery Automobile Co’s Jaecoo proving a hit with consumers.

While volumes are not as high in Germany, Chinese companies are also gaining ground in Europe’s largest car market, picking up a 6.4% market share there in August, according to Dataforce.

“Even if their market share is comparably low to other markets, the sheer size of the German market makes that move, however, very attractive,” said Dataforce analyst Julian Litzinger.

See also: ECB launches key link between blockchain and euro payment system

Across Europe, EV sales are climbing, in part due to the return of incentives in countries like Germany. That is taking a toll on some European manufacturers because those models tend to have lower margins. Volkswagen AG last week said the uplift is weighing on profitability, particularly at the Volkswagen passenger car and Audi brands.

The Paris car show next month will give European brands an opportunity to showcase their fightback on home turf. For Chinese marques, it is a chance to lay out plans to target the premium end of the market, having already made inroads with mass-market buyers.

title: Hong Kong’s Paul Chan rejects ‘race to bottom’ with Singapore
article:
(Sept 23): Hong Kong will focus on enhancing its core strengths rather than entering a race to outbid Singapore with generous tax breaks, as the rival Asian finance hubs compete for wealthy investors and global talent, Financial Secretary Paul Chan said.

“We do not want to race to the bottom, but at the same time we need to be competitive,” Chan said in an interview with Bloomberg TV on Wednesday.

Earlier this year, Hong Kong proposed tax breaks, including a broad expansion of tax exemptions on so-called carried interest — a share of investment profits that can mean big bucks for star fund managers. The move prompted Singapore to roll out similar incentives to maintain its appeal to fund managers.

Chan said the government is working hard to implement the tax breaks “within this year.” He also touted the city’s access to the mainland Chinese market, availability of talent and quality of life, among its advantages over rival Singapore.

Hong Kong is seeking to strengthen its position as a financial centre while accelerating investment in technology under its new five-year plan, unveiled by chief executive John Lee last week.

Chan said the Northern Metropolis, the development area bordering the Chinese economic powerhouse of Shenzhen, will be a major engine of growth in the “next decade or two”.

See also: Radiant World sent Mizuho fake Glencore email, court filing says

He also defended the Hong Kong dollar’s long-term role as authorities promote wider use of the yuan, including in public expenditure, which he described as taking advantage of the lower costs of borrowing in the currency. Chan said the government had “no intention” of changing its peg to the dollar.

On financial markets, Chan said attracting quality companies was the key to improving liquidity after a surge in initial public offerings. He said further regulatory action would depend on market conditions, while stressing that due diligence, credibility and investor confidence remained priorities.

Chan did not confirm whether US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent would attend a gathering by Apec financial ministers next month, saying “we welcome everyone” and that the government was awaiting a response from those invited to join.

title: SoftBank offers record yields on jumbo junk bonds in AI push — Bloomberg
article:
(Sept 23): Billionaire Masayoshi Son’s SoftBank Group Corp kicked off what’s set to be one of the largest corporate junk bond sales ever as the Japanese conglomerate offers record yields to entice investors into helping fund its unprecedented investments in artificial intelligence (AI).

One of the world’s biggest investors in AI, SoftBank started marketing the multi-part deal, with price talk underway for the dollar portion, according to a person familiar with the matter who asked not to be identified as the discussions are private. The group aims to raise the equivalent of more than US$11 billion ($14.03 billion) in the offering that includes a US$10 billion dollar part and a €1 billion (US$1.1 billion or $1.46 billion) portion.

The offering is the latest in a flurry of activity by SoftBank in debt markets this year to help fund commitments nearing US$65 billion to ChatGPT creator OpenAI, as well as more M&A in the sector. The moves have put the Japanese investment firm at the epicentre of debt-fuelled bets on artificial intelligence, at a time when the promise of the technology has riveted global markets even as safety concerns about the industry have flared.

SoftBank is offering record yields on the dollar portion at this stage, though those figures could change by the time the deal actually prices. The conglomerate is marketing US$1 billion of 3.5-year bonds to yield 8.75% to 8.875%, US$4.5 billion of 5.5-year securities at 9.375% to 9.5% and the same amount of 7.5-year securities at 9.75% to 9.875%, the person said. Those would be the highest-ever levels for SoftBank dollar bonds of those maturities, according to data compiled by Bloomberg.

Price talk for the euro portion is still due to come later, people familiar with the matter said.

See also: Alibaba to add data centres in Europe, Middle East in AI push

The group isn’t alone in storming markets for funding, with global AI-related debt issuance already topping US$575 billion in 2026, according to a recent report by Goldman Sachs Group Inc credit strategists.

Son has downplayed concerns about investments in AI infrastructure, and said earlier this year he expects AI-related industries to account for 20% of global output by 2040, equivalent to US$46 trillion.

The flood of AI funding in global financial markets, however, has made some bond investors uneasy. Their concern is that the ever-growing pile of the debt threatens to cause a hangover for markets if the technology fails to pay off for the firms that are making the biggest investments.

See also: China’s AI trade favours global winners over local champions

With price talk for the shortest SoftBank tranche of 3.5 years starting at 8.75% to 8.875%, if the company ended up paying within that range it would be closer to the average market yield of 8.5% on B-rated notes in the US market, several levels below the Japanese company’s own rating of BB+, the highest speculative-grade score from S&P, according to data compiled by Bloomberg.

Broadly, the average yield on dollar bonds rated in the B zone is 7.5% and 6.55% for those rated in the BB area, Bloomberg indices show.

title: Seatrium completes seventh LNGC to FSRU conversion for Karpowership
article:
Mainboard-listed Seatrium has completed its seventh liquified natural gas carrier (LNGC) to floating, storage and regasification unit (FSRU) conversion for power generator Karpowership, according to a Sept 23 announcement.

The conversions are part of an eight-year programme that began in 2018. All vessels were converted at Seatrium’s Admiralty Yard and involved complex cryogenic, marine and gas-handling systems integration works.

The FSRUs will operate alongside Karpowership’s global Powership fleet, supplying clean, reliable feed gas to floating power plants, as part of Karpowership’s integrated LNG-to-power value chain.

Alvin Gan, executive vice president of repairs and upgrades at Seatrium, says: “The completion of the programme reflects the strength of our longstanding partnership with Karpowership and reinforces Seatrium's leadership in FSRU conversions and offshore energy infrastructure solutions. We value Karpowership's continued trust and look forward to expanding our collaboration beyond FSRU projects, including next-generation Powerships and offshore energy solutions, as we support our customers’ ambitions to meet the rapidly growing global energy demand.”

Ersen Ayanoglu, assistant general manager, LNG investments global shipbuilding, Karpowership, says: “The successful completion of our seventh FSRU conversion reflects the strength of our long-standing partnership with Seatrium. Time and again, Seatrium has demonstrated its ability to overcome complex technical and operational challenges, transforming ambitious plans into successful project outcomes.”

Last year, both companies signed a letter of intent (LOI) covering the conversion of three LNG carriers into FSRUs, one of which has since materialised into a contract award for the LNG tanker Karadeniz conversion project. The LOI also includes the potential integration of up to six new-generation Powerships.

“Having delivered over 90% of the world's FSU and FSRU conversions, Seatrium combines deep engineering expertise, integrated yard capabilities and execution excellence to navigate complexity and deliver certainty for our customers,” adds Gan.

To date, Seatrium has successfully delivered 22 FSRU, floating liquified natural gas vessels and floating storage unit conversion projects worldwide.

At around 11.50 am on Sept 23, shares in Seatrium are trading at $2.13, down two cents or 1%.
